title: S-Gan Villa
summary: An ageing single-storey house re-imagined as a calm contemporary home — designed and built end-to-end by our team in under six months.
body: An ageing single-storey house in a dense Chennai neighbourhood, re-imagined as a calm contemporary home. The existing load-bearing structure was surveyed, stripped back and re-serviced, then crowned with a new first-floor bedroom suite under a timber-rafter and clay-tile gable roof that gives the street front a warm, traditional silhouette.

Kavinan Design Studio carried the project end-to-end — measured survey, 3D design, working drawings, procurement, site execution and handover — in under six months. New wiring and plumbing were concealed, floors re-laid, and every room re-planned for light and storage.

Inside, a modular kitchen with fluted-glass shutters and patterned backsplash, a floating TV wall, full-height timber wardrobes and a spa-like bath with a freestanding tub complete a home that looks entirely new while keeping the memory of the old one.
features: New first-floor suite with clay-tile gable roof
Modular kitchen, wardrobes & TV wall joinery

title: Strata — Yercaud
summary: Like layers of rock on a hillside, Strata stacks offset volumes up a steep Yercaud slope — eight named suites, timber jaali screens and terraces opening to forest and valley.
body: Like layers of rock on a hillside, Strata stacks a series of offset volumes up a steep Yercaud slope. Each level steps and cantilevers to open its rooms to the forest and valley, while pitched timber roofs, deep balconies and curved glazing respond to the cool, misty hill climate.

The latest design revision (R2) sharpens the identity of Strata Luxury Stay: crisp white volumes, slender sloping roof canopies, timber jaali screens that filter light and give privacy to the suites, planted terraces and a bridge-like circulation stair linking the stacked blocks.

Eight individually named suites — the Moss, Pine and Ridge Strata Nests, the Mist, Fern, Canopy and Brook Strata Vistas and the Summit Strata Signature — sit above a stilt parking level. Guests arrive at a reception lounge, and the whole building culminates in a dining hall and kitchens on the top floor with panoramic views.

title: Mr. Aravindhan Residence
summary: A dated two-storey house given a crisp new identity without rebuilding it.
body: A dated two-storey house given a crisp new identity without rebuilding it. The proposal keeps the existing frame and re-composes the façade around a cantilevered sloping canopy, a projecting first-floor balcony and deep timber-slatted gates, finished in a restrained palette of powder blue and charcoal.

Concealed wall-washers and up-lights make the house glow at dusk, while new compound walls and planting tidy the street edge. Inside, a back-lit marble-finish TV wall with fluted timber and display niches sets the tone for the living spaces.
features: Façade upgrade on the existing structure

title: Residences across Tamil Nadu
summary: Individual homes tuned to plot, budget and family — confident street presence, practical, ventilated and Vastu-aware plans.
body: A selection of individual homes across Tamil Nadu, each tuned to its plot, budget and family. Strong framing elements, natural stone and timber cladding, and carefully placed openings give modest footprints a confident street presence, while plans stay practical, ventilated and Vastu-aware.

**Mr. RK Residence, Dindigul** — a two-storey home with stacked natural-stone cladding, a deep black portal frame and a timber-lined porch that glows at dusk. A slatted roof pergola and landscaped front edge complete the street elevation.
**Mr. Dinesh Residence, Theni** — slender vertical glazing, timber accents and a lit fin wall give a compact house a strong vertical identity among the banana groves.
**Mr. Kannan Residence, Mayiladuthurai** — a single-storey family home with a framed entrance portal, timber-clad accents and a tall feature column that lifts the low street elevation.

**R.V. Bhavanam (Mr. Lokesh Residence), Swamimalai** — a two-storey home in bold festive colours — a red frame and a yellow stair tower — that gives the family a joyful, instantly recognisable address.

title: Lakeside Farmhouse
summary: A weekend retreat set into a wooded, sloping lakeside site, with the landscape designed as part of the architecture.
body: A weekend retreat set into a wooded, sloping lakeside site. A glazed double-height entrance volume and a long timber-clad pavilion sit lightly in the landscape, opening the living spaces to the water and the forest edge.

The landscape is designed as part of the architecture: a gravel forecourt for arrival, terraced lawns, flowering borders and a winding drive that steps down the slope towards the lake, lit softly at night.
features: Terraced lawns following the natural slope
Lakeside views from every living space

title: Mixed Use Development
summary: Three residential towers rise from a landscaped commercial podium, linked by sky-bridges and glazed circulation cores.
body: Three high-rise residential towers rise from a landscaped commercial podium. Cylindrical glazed circulation cores and aerial sky-bridges link the towers at upper levels, giving residents shared terraces and alternative routes between blocks.

A palm-lined ramped drive separates vehicles from pedestrians, while podium gardens, generous balconies and a disciplined façade rhythm bring greenery, daylight and cross-ventilation into a dense urban plot.
features: Three towers on a shared podium

title: TATA Corporate Office
summary: A curved, fully glazed office block wrapped in blue solar fins, with a sweeping cantilevered entrance canopy.
body: A curved, fully glazed office block wrapped in a rhythm of blue vertical fins and horizontal louvres that shade the workfloors and express the brand colour. A sweeping cantilevered canopy on slender columns marks the entrance and shelters the drop-off.
A solid brand tower and a glazed service core anchor the composition against the hills, while open-plan floors behind the curved façade allow flexible workplace layouts.
features: Curved glass façade with solar fins

title: Thozhi Women's Hostel
summary: A safe, bright and efficient residence for working women, with a bold terracotta-banded corner volume.
body: A safe, bright and efficient residence for working women. The three-storey block is organised around a sheltered entrance porch and a clear central stair, with rooms arranged for privacy, cross-ventilation and easy supervision.
A bold terracotta-banded corner volume, tall vertical glazing lighting the circulation and framed windows give rhythm and identity to an otherwise economical building.
features: Secure single entry with sheltered porch

title: Alpha Multispeciality Hospital
summary: A multi-storey hospital with a calm, legible presence — timber-toned louvres shading the wards, planning that follows clinical flow.
body: A multi-storey hospital with a calm, legible presence. Angled frames of timber-toned louvres drift across the façade, shading ward windows from the sun and giving the building a memorable identity on the street, while the clearly expressed ground floor separates the main and emergency entrances.

Planning follows clinical flow — public reception and outpatient areas at the base, wards and treatment above. Interiors favour clean, washable surfaces and natural light: a generous reception spine, warm consultation lounges and well-organised day-care wards.

title: Architectural Institute
summary: A campus for an architecture school that teaches through its own buildings — brick, jaali, folded steel and daylight.
body: A campus for an architecture school that teaches through its own buildings. Exposed brick academic blocks with jaali screens filter light and air into classrooms, while an auditorium under an undulating roof gives the campus a civic heart.

A studio wing of folded steel frames and full-height glazing floods the drawing studios with daylight, and an open-air amphitheatre beneath a steel lattice canopy hosts juries and events — all tied together by shaded pergola walks and courts.

title: Visual & Performing Arts Centre
summary: An elliptical drum of punched openings housing a large auditorium for music, dance and theatre.
body: An elliptical drum of punched openings houses a large auditorium for music, dance and theatre. The pure, curving form gives the building presence, while the regular window rhythm keeps it calm and timeless.

A dark, sculptural foyer prepares the audience for the performance; the auditorium is planned with raked seating, clear sightlines and acoustic wall treatment. Landscaped boulder gardens and broad entrance steps soften the arrival.

title: ISRO Campus Visualisation
summary: A visionary master plan where ring-shaped, green-roofed buildings orbit landscaped courts like planetary paths.
body: A visionary master plan for a space research and visitor campus. Ring-shaped buildings with green roofs orbit landscaped courts, echoing planetary paths and keeping each department connected to the next.

Launch-vehicle replicas, an arrival boulevard, extensive tree cover and wind turbines frame a campus about science, exploration and sustainability — visualised as a full aerial and eye-level walkthrough.

title: Elidi Stadia
summary: A stadium conceived as an unfolding flower — white shell canopies overlap like petals around the bowl.
body: A stadium conceived as an unfolding flower. Sculptural white shell canopies overlap like petals around the bowl, shading the stands while letting light and breeze pass through the gaps between them.

A full athletics track and football pitch sit within the bowl, with colour-coded seating tiers. Outside, reflecting pools, paved promenades, practice courts and landscaped lawns turn the stadium grounds into a public park on non-event days.
features: Grounds open as a public park

title: National Maritime Heritage Complex
summary: A master plan celebrating India's maritime history, organised around a radial plaza laid out like a ship's wheel.
body: A master plan that celebrates India's maritime history. A radial plaza laid out like a ship's wheel organises the galleries and pavilions, each spoke leading visitors to a different chapter of the story.
A heritage promenade lined with lamp posts connects the plaza to full-scale ship exhibits along the water, and a dramatic illuminated gateway marks the entry to the complex.

title: Pavilion at CSA
summary: A forecourt canopy built from hundreds of small timber modules, branching like trees into a layered roof.
body: A canopy for the school's forecourt, built up from hundreds of small timber modules. Tree-like columns branch into a layered roof that filters sunlight like a forest canopy, creating a shaded gathering space at the threshold of the campus.
The modular system allows the pavilion to be prefabricated, assembled by students and adapted over time.

title: Pond Park at Sivakasi
summary: The edge of a town pond reclaimed as a family promenade — lawns, play, a kiosk and an illuminated landmark.
body: The edge of a town pond reclaimed as a public promenade. Paved walks with heritage-style lamp posts and railings wrap the water, with lawns, planters and colourful seating along the way.
A children's play area, an ice-cream kiosk and an illuminated star sculpture — the park's selfie point — make it a family destination from morning walks to evening outings.

title: Mr. Jithu's Residence
summary: Bedroom interiors explored across a family of colourways so the client could choose a mood before anything was built.
body: Bedroom interiors explored across a family of colourways — sage, forest green, terracotta and ivory — so the client could choose a mood before anything was built.

Each variant keeps the same crafted elements: a ginkgo-leaf metal feature wall, back-lit mirror and display niches, a glossy full-height wardrobe, a compact study desk and a layered cove ceiling with concealed lighting.

title: Church Interior
summary: Two design options for a church sanctuary — warm timber panelling, gilded capitals and arched niches framing the altar.
body: Two design options for a church sanctuary. Warm timber panelling, gilded capitals and arched niches frame the altar and bring a sense of dignity and warmth to the space.
Option A centres the crucifix on a deep maroon backdrop with gothic niches for statues; Option B sets it before a geometric stained-glass window flooded with daylight, beneath a chandelier.

images.caption: Option A — crucifix on maroon backdrop

title: Archdais Interior Competition
summary: Traditional South Indian colour and craft brought into a contemporary home — a bath that becomes a courtyard.
body: A competition entry that brings traditional South Indian colour and craft into a contemporary home. The bath becomes a courtyard: a stone water wall, skylight, pebbles and a stepping-stone garden turn a daily routine into a calm ritual.
A brick-and-jaali living room glows under a coffered ceiling, and the kitchen pairs dark timber with a green-framed garden window. Hand-painted motifs tie the rooms together.

title: Cubro — Operating Theatre
summary: A complete, fabrication-ready working-drawing package for a modular operating theatre fit-out.
body: A complete working-drawing package for a modular operating theatre fit-out. The set covers the general arrangement, floor and reflected ceiling plans, sections and wall elevations, and the nurse-station desk set-out.

Every drawing coordinates HPL wall panels, the laminar-flow ceiling, monitors, pass-boxes, medical gas and electrical services to millimetre precision, ready for factory fabrication and site installation.

title: The Pitau — Travertine Façade
summary: Panel-by-panel set-out drawings for a travertine façade — every stone numbered, every curve resolved in 3D.
body: Panel-by-panel set-out drawings for a travertine stone façade. Every stone is numbered and dimensioned across plans, elevations and curved balcony profiles.
3D views of the curved panels resolve the tricky geometry before cutting, giving the fabricator and installer a precise, buildable package.

title: Mr. Prabu Residence
summary: A courtyard home in Kumbakonam that brings the warmth of traditional Tamil architecture into everyday modern living.
body: At the heart of the house is an open-to-sky courtyard — the mutram — framed by turned timber pillars and a carved timber cornice. Daylight falls into a sunken court with a stone planter at its centre, and every room opens back towards it.

The palette is rooted in the region: patterned floor tiles, a deep green dado, warm ivory walls, dark timber doors with brass detailing and a red arched niche carrying a hand-drawn kolam motif. Jaali windows and high clerestory openings keep the interiors bright and well ventilated.

The living room pairs this heritage character with contemporary comfort — a dark coffered timber ceiling, soft upholstered seating and a slim media wall suspended on brass chains, a quiet nod to the traditional oonjal swing.
